description: Vertical 125B housing family and the one-piece OEM QuickMount B1 plate that covers it. The plate is reproduced from Warwick's own Type B1 sheets; the third-party plate this project used to carry is kept beside the output as dwg/125B_quickmount-ORIGINAL.stl.

provenance.source: vendor pages; the plate is 2.5-4 mm longer and 5 mm wider than either housing

mount.structure: one 3 mm plate carrying two integral C-loop clips, one at each end, with two screw patterns at every end: four Ø4 clearance holes and four Ø3.5 screw-head snaps, plus one Ø3.5 hole on each side
mount.datum: plate bottom-face centre. +X across the 67 mm width, +Y along the 125.5 mm length, +Z from the board-facing face toward the pedal, so the plate occupies z = 0..3 and the clips hang at z < 0

end_window.note: cut through the plate and open to the end edge. It is the same opening the A/E plates cut for an inserted retainer, carried out to the end instead of closed: it takes the clip's mouth and the free blade, so the plate fuses to the post alone and the loop stays open

snap.relief: both sheets draw four radial slots round each snap hole, so the fingers can pass a screw head; the repro carries the bore and the spot-face only

clips.attachment: both arms run the full plate thickness. The post finishes inside the plate's own material and fuses to it; the blade passes up through the end window with 1.30 clear a side and finishes flush with the plate's top face, still free to flex the ledge. So the lip reads level with the plate, as it does on a plate that takes an inserted retainer
clips.mouth: toward the board-facing face and open right through the plate, because the window is cut away over it
clips.pitch_check: 95.0 is 2.84 of the board's 33.43 pitch, so the pair does not land on rib centres. The third-party plate reads 95.5 and the drawing reads 95.0, so the whole-pitch rule in the retainer config was an assumption about the A/E plates, not a fact about B1

oem_variant.what: Warwick's own clip is slit across its width into three fingers, 4.5, 9.6 and 4.5 with two 1.7 slots, because a carbon-fibre moulding needs the relief to flex. The printed plate is one solid section instead, so the slits are not cut into it.

provenance.source: the three wall bands and two 1.7 gaps across the clip in the face view of ref/QuickMount-TypeB1-alt.pdf, scaled against its 45 callout

fabrication.print_orientation: pedal face down, so both C-loops rise off the plate
fabrication.supports: none; the mouth's ceiling then bridges 13.0 between the post and the blade
fabrication.note: printed the other way up the loops would sit inside the bed

derived.lobe_circle: r 6.60 about (29.4, 56.15) is tangent to the 125.5 end edge and reaches x = 36.00, which makes the 72.0 overall width
derived.window_is_the_slot: the window's inboard wall lands on the clip's mouth wall, 62.75 - 21.9 = 40.85 against 47.5 - 6.5 = 41.00, so the opening is the 24 mm slot the A/E plates cut for an inserted retainer, carried out to the end edge instead of closed. That is what leaves the loop open and lets the lip come up flush
derived.blade_clearance_mm: (24.6 - 22.0) / 2 = 1.30 either side, the same fit the A/E plates give an inserted retainer in their 24 slot
derived.side_edge_run_mm: the straight side runs from where each lobe crosses it, 50.98, down to the 4.5 boss at 29.92
derived.hole_pair_mm: an Ø4 at (22.5, 56.75) and its snap at (29.5, 56.0) are 7.04 apart, so the two patterns sit side by side in the same corner lobe
derived.end_margin_mm: 62.75 - 56.75 = 6.00 to the Ø4 row and 62.75 - 56.00 = 6.75 to the snap row
derived.mid_hole_chain: 23.25 above the bottom snap row puts the side holes at y = -32.75, and the alt sheet's 29.5 from there to the end edge closes on 62.25 against 62.75 for the drawn end, so the two sheets agree to 0.5

measured.how: the alt sheet is vector, so its callouts fix a scale of 1.9135 pt/mm and every unprinted feature is then read off the geometry. 45.01 for the printed 45, 113.51 for 113.5, 3.50 for Ø3.5, 4.00 for Ø4 and 60.5 for the printed 60 all reproduce inside 0.9 percent, which puts the scale at about 0.3 mm over the whole plate
measured.lobe_centre: circle fits to the lobe arcs put the four centres at x ±29.35 and y ±56.0 with r 6.75 on the outer stroke and 6.46 on the inner, so 6.6 mid-stroke; adopted as r 6.6 about (29.4, 56.15) so the printed 72 x 125.5 closes exactly
measured.end_edge: the face view's end edge runs out to 26.65 off centre and sits 0.25 below the lobe tops; the 0.25 jog is a moulding step and is not modelled
measured.end_window: 24.59 wide from the gap between the drawn end-edge segments and 21.9 deep from the full-width line at 34.8..35.4, which is where the plate's material resumes and the clip's mouth wall stands
measured.clip_attachment: the loop reads as a free C in both the face view and the isometric: the window is carried from the end edge down over the mouth and the blade, so the plate fuses to the post alone. The three lines across the clip in the face view are the OEM's slit fingers, not plate material
measured.clip_envelope: the side view gives an outer width of 18.4, a mouth of 14.1, an 18.5 drop and the ledge 4.0 below the plate, all within 0.6 of the retainer section in commons, which is what this plate uses
measured.clip_positions: the two loops read at y ±47.5 from the side view, 95.0 apart

outline_length_and_width.source: 125.5 on the alt side view, 72 on the alt end view and on the Type B1 front view, 67 between the straight sides on both B1 sheets

corner_lobes.source: lobe arcs scaled off ref/QuickMount-TypeB1-alt.pdf about the snap centres; not printed

end_window.source: face view and isometric of ref/QuickMount-TypeB1-alt.pdf; not printed

clearance_holes.source: 45 x 113.5 and Ø4 printed on the alt sheet; 59 between the snaps on the Type B1 sheet

snap_holes.source: Ø3.5 and 112 printed on the alt sheet

side_holes.source: 60 printed on the alt sheet, 23.25 printed on the Type B1 sheet, 29.5 printed on the alt sheet

counterbore.source: 1.5 printed on section B-B of the Type B1 sheet; the 6.8 diameter is scaled off that section

counterbore_face.source: the recesses open on the clip side, where the screw heads have to sit clear of the board and where section B-B's hatch shows the step; no sheet prints which face

spotfaces.source: 5.8 rings round the Ø3.5 holes, scaled off the alt sheet; the 1.5 depth is taken from section B-B

clips.source: section from ../commons/cfg/retainer.json, guarded by calipers on an owned Type E; placement scaled off the alt side view

thickness.source: 3 printed on section B-B of the Type B1 sheet

material.note: the plate prints in the same filament as the retainer, so the presets are referenced from commons rather than restated

verification.method: read every callout on both B1 sheets, scale the vector alt sheet against its own dims, then check the drawing against the model the generator builds. The printed callouts govern; a scaled reading only fills in what neither sheet prints.

cross_checks.verdict: the two patterns are concentric per end and differ only in pitch, which is why every corner carries a plain hole and a star hole side by side
scales to 60.5, and 23.25 up from the snap row lands at y = -32.75, which 29.5 below the end edge confirms to 0.5
the drawing and the third-party plate agree to 0.5, so the whole-pitch assumption in the retainer config does not hold for B1
the third-party plate is mirrored the same way at 95.5, so the lay-out agrees even where its section does not
the drawn silhouette is the retainer moulding to within 0.6, so the commons section is used rather than a new one measured off a 1 percent raster

verification.fit_policy: dimensions printed on either B1 sheet govern. Values only obtainable by scaling the sheets are adopted to 0.1 mm and carry that scale's 0.3 mm uncertainty. The clip section is not re-derived here: it belongs to commons/cfg/retainer.json, where calipers and six OEM sheets already settle it.

open_questions: The Ø3.5 features are drawn with four radial relief slots so the fingers can pass a screw head. The repro carries the bore and its 5.8 spot-face but not the slots, so it grips by screw tension rather than by snap.

Which face carries the 1.5 recess is not printed. It is modelled on the clip side, where the screw heads have to sit clear of the board; the pedal side stays flat so the plate beds against the pedal's base plate. That leaves the pedal-facing face as the one to check with a straight edge on a real plate.

The OEM clip is a carbon-fibre moulding slit into fingers across its width. This plate prints the same section solid in PETG: the fingers exist to stiffen a brittle composite, and a solid section flexes further before it yields. The slitted version is kept as ref/125B_oem_clip_fingers.stl for comparison, not for printing.
pedal_riser still inherits the old 120 x 65 measured base. That base is the third-party plate, not this one, and needs revisiting before the riser is generated.
notes: Type B1 covers vertical 125B housings across Keeley, EQD, JHS, Mooer, Seymour Duncan, Friedman, Wampler and Walrus, so one plate serves the family.

The clip is modelled solid across its 22 mm width. The OEM part is carbon-fibre reinforced and slit into fingers; that is a way of making a stiff composite flex, and a PETG print of the same section bends further from the arch alone, so reproducing the slits would only cut the section that carries the pedal.
A separate 3-4 mm adhesive mat sits board-side, between plate and board; the ledge depth in the retainer section is set by the board's sheet, not by the mat.
The clip section is referenced, never restated: a corrected wall or ledge in commons/cfg/retainer.json changes this plate on the next run.
